### 📋 LEGAL PRELIMINARY REPORT

* **Categories:** SEXUAL ASSAULT
* **Involved Party Type:** faculty

#### ⚖️ STATUTORY FRAMEWORK
**Governing Acts:**
* Indian Penal Code (IPC) Sections 375-376 (Rape & Sexual Assault)

**Key Legal Provisions:**
* **Section 375** (Indian Penal Code): Rape
* **Section 376** (Indian Penal Code): Punishment for rape
* **Section 376A** (Indian Penal Code): Rape by husband on wife during separation
* **Section 3** (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012): Punishment for penetrative sexual assault on a child
* **Section 5** (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012): Punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault

#### 📝 ACTIONABLE PROCEDURES
1. Go to nearest police station or emergency services immediately
2. Report to female police officer if available (women can request this)
3. File FIR and get copy within 30 minutes
4. Do NOT bathe or change clothes before medical examination
5. Get medical examination at government hospital within 24 hours
6. Collect detailed medical report documenting injury, semen, DNA
7. Obtain photographs of all injuries
8. Provide complete statement to investigating officer
9. Inform police about any CCTV footage or witnesses
10. Request police to preserve all physical evidence
11. Apply for victim compensation under Victim Compensation Scheme
12. Request counseling support from NGOs
13. File anticipatory bail application if threatened by accused
14. Intimate court about threats or pressure to withdraw complaint

2. Approach internal complaints committee (ICC) if in workplace/college

5. Request time-bound investigation
6. File complaint with District Commission for Women if no action

#### 🏷️ CASE SUMMARY
* **Categories:** CYBER BULLYING

#### ⚖️ STATUTORY FRAMEWORK
**Governing Acts:**
* Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000 (Cyber Crime)

**Key Legal Provisions:**
* **Section 499** (Indian Penal Code): Defamation
* **Section 503-506** (Indian Penal Code): Criminal intimidation and threats
* **Section 66E** (Information Technology Act, 2000): Violation of privacy
* **Section 509** (Indian Penal Code): Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman
* **Section 67** (Information Technology Act, 2000): Publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form

#### 📝 ACTIONABLE PROCEDURES
1. Collect and preserve screenshots, URLs, timestamps and message headers of abusive content
2. File complaint with local police cybercrime cell or file online on state police cyber portals
3. Provide links to social media posts and request takedown from the platform
4. File FIR under relevant IPC sections (e.g., 499, 503, 506, 509) and IT Act provisions as applicable
5. Request police to obtain subscriber information and preserve evidence from the platform/ISP
6. Request interim protection orders or blocking orders against harassers
7. Report abusive accounts to the social media platform and follow up for escalation
8. Seek civil remedies for defamation or privacy violations (send notice to platform/accused)
9. Obtain legal advice for takedown notices and cease-and-desist communications
10. Keep record of all communications with police and platform; seek victim support services if needed

* **Section 406** (Indian Penal Code): Punishment for criminal breach of trust

laws.title: Identity theft
laws.description: Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly makes use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh.

laws.title: Cheating by personation by using computer resource
laws.description: Whoever by means of computer resource or communications device cheats by personation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh.

laws.title: Defamation
laws.description: Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm his reputation or knowing it to be likely to harm his reputation, commits defamation.

laws.title: Punishment for defamation
laws.description: Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

laws.title: Punishment for criminal breach of trust
laws.description: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property in his capacity of a public servant or by virtue of any law for the time being in force, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of that property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine.
